name: SageAttention: Accurate 8-Bit Attention for Plug-and-play Inference Acceleration
problem: Attention itself can be quantised to cut the memory traffic of the QK^T and PV matmuls, but naive INT8 quantisation of attention loses accuracy because the softmax output contains large channel-wise outliers that a single per-tensor scale cannot represent.
mechanism: Two-level smoothing. Smooth K by moving a per-channel maximum out of the value matrices and folding it into the following scale, and smooth P similarly using a property of the softmax (x - max(x) = softmax(x) >= 0), so both operands have quantisation-friendly distributions. Then quantise the smoothed QK^T and PV matmuls to INT8 with per-tensor scales. The smoothing folds are algebraically absorbed into the surrounding weights, so the model is not retrained.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): OPS outperform FlashAttention2 by about 2.1x and xformers by about 2.7x, with superior accuracy to FlashAttention3, and almost no end-to-end metrics loss across language, image and video generation models. Baseline class named (FA2, xformers); OPS is the paper's own throughput metric for attention, not decode tok/s.
